about: MUTATING — delete the forge branches whose cars landed BEFORE the database switch, on TWO sources of evidence — the ARCHIVE database's job records, by exactly the arriving train's sweep rule, and the forge's own PULL-REQUEST ANCESTRY (infra/forge/sweep-archive-branches.sh <mode> <namespace> <archive-db>). Backlog dfd83788, measured 2026-09-17: boss orient listed 50 forge heads no packet claims — the arrival sweep deletes a landed car's branch on the JOB RECORD's evidence (train.rs deletable_branches + sweep_guard), and every car that landed before the 2026-09-16 23:55Z switch lives in the archive database, not the system of record, so the sweep can never see them. The rule is the sweep's, which is David's protocol decision for arrivals (train PRs squash-merge, so the job record is the proof), applied unchanged: a branch comes off iff a closed, merged ship-a-change car in the archive names it (metadata.branch with boarded_head, or a rerail_origins entry with its head) AND the branch's current head on the forge equals the recorded head. THE SECOND SOURCE (backlog 2c10a25d, measured 2026-09-17 08:00Z): the first dry run planned 6 of the 50 because the cars of trains #384–#411 closed inside the converge hold and after the switch, so no database recorded their landing — the forge did: refs/pull/N/head is train PR N's assembled consist, main carries the squash commit titled '… (#N)' when N merged, and a branch head that is an ANCESTOR of a merged PR's head landed with it (37 of the 50). So a forge head the archive did not plan is planned with evidence pull-request and the newest merged PR number; a head also in an OPEN PR is still deletable when a merged one contains it (merged wins); a head only in unmerged PRs is not evidence. Every delete is leased to the head the evidence vouches for (push --delete --force-with-lease), so a branch that moves between the read and the push is refused by the forge and recorded failed. Two defects of the same run, fixed: gone is a COUNT (1,014 gone names made a 184 KB record the runner cut at 102,400 bytes, taking the plan off the packet — a gone branch is nothing to act on), and the live system of record's open ship-a-change cars are read through boss-sor-read as a read-scoped actor so a head an open car names is reported live, never unrecorded and never planned (a follow-up car branched from a landed head is live work); an unreadable live record is a refusal. Moved = kept and named; a claim with no head = kept and named; a head no source claims = kept and named (an abandoned attempt or a never-filed branch — a human's decision, listed for one). THE BOUNDS, each a refusal that changes nothing: the arguments (namespace boss or boss-<name>, never boss-dev; a plain lowercase database name); the archive must NOT be the database Secret boss-secrets/database-url names (parsed in a variable, THE PASSWORD IS NEVER PRINTED, a test asserts it) — that is the live system of record and the live sweep owns it; ONE read-only psql round trip through the kubectl-exec door tenant-census uses; the heads read with ls-remote on the converged checkout's forgejo remote, whose URL (it may carry a token) is never printed; the live record read once through boss-sor-read (absent, refusing, wrong-shaped or cut at its limit = refusal); the pull heads fetched once through the same remote under the checkout's lock into the verb's own ref namespace, never refs/remotes; only a branch name of the shape [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/-]* is ever handed to the push, as the full ref. --dry-run prints the plan and pushes nothing; --for-real is a human's decision to file: one leased delete push per planned branch, each READ BACK with ls-remote (a forge answer is not a forge effect) and recorded. The verdict line prints FIRST (the runner keeps 100 KB) — recorded, planned, by_archive, by_pr, deleted, moved, unrecorded, live, gone — then the JSON record, then the per-branch lines. THE DECISION (backlog a12736b1, 2026-09-18): the for-real sweep e96e5e60 deleted the 40 it could prove landed and the dry run after it (a2d0b0fc) still kept 10 — 2 moved, 8 unrecorded — 'a human's decision'; the human had decided (design 7fc3970b, answered on packet 2604d814's design-review by David, 'Delete them all') and the verb had no door to carry it out. The OPTIONAL fourth arg `decision` names that packet by full job id: the verb reads it through boss-sor-read as the same read-scoped actor and requires a backlog-item or design-doc whose design-review (or review) step is completed, not declined, with an answer or resolutions — anything else is refused naming the packet and the missing fact, and nothing is deleted. With a qualifying decision the moved and unrecorded branches are deleted too, each named 'by decision <id>', leased to the forge's head and read back absent like the rest; a live car's branch and an OPEN pr-train's train/ branch (read only when a decision is given) are never candidates, and main never is. A dry run with a decision plans the decided set and pushes nothing. The verdict line carries by_decision=<n> and decision=<id> when one was given.
